The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Bitcoin hits $80,000 for the first time since May as crypto recovery accelerates. BTC has now surged 38% following its June plunge as shifting U.S. Treasury policy helped bring buyers back to crypto, rejuvenating ETF demand. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin nears $80,000, but analysts say the next pullback will be key. Analysts say consolidation could strengthen bitcoin’s rally, while thin trading above $80,000 may set up sharper price moves. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Crypto political group details list of U.S. congressional allies its backing this year. Stand With Crypto, a member group that rates the crypto friendliness of politicians, is supporting 32 U.S. House incumbents, with more endorsements coming. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Coinbase debuts tokenized stocks on Base network, joining race to bring equities on blockchain. The crypto exchange is starting with tokenized versions of Apple, Nvidia, Meta and Alphabet, issued under its new Abu Dhabi framework. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Tom Lee's Bitmine buys $81 million of ETH in largest weekly haul since early July. The treasury firm stepped up its ETH buying as Tom Lee said the crypto’s 30% weekly rally could signal a larger move ahead. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

New Solana vote could ramp daily SOL burns to $800,000 and slow new token creation. Two of the three proposals would reduce SOL supply growth by speeding up Solana’s inflation decline and raising daily fee burns from about 650 SOL to as much as 9,000 SOL. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $80,420 with a +4.43% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,497.78 with a +2.48% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.description:

The Stablecoin Statement specifically addresses stablecoins that are designed to maintain a stable value relative to the US dollar (USD) on a one-for-one basis, [...] On September 19, 2025, Treasury issued an Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (ANPRM), seeking public comment related to its implementation of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins (GENIUS) Act, a comprehensive framework for the federal regulation of payment stablecoins enacted on July 18, 2025.

Read more on Latham's Global Fintech & Digital Assets Blog. The GENIUS Act, enacted by Congress in July 2025, created a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins whereby a subsidiary of an insured depository institution could be approved to issue payment stablecoins.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation in the United States has historically been fragmented, with federal agencies applying different interpretations based on the nature and use of each asset. That splintered approach began to change in 2025, when Congress passed legislation to establish a clearer framework for stablecoins and digital asset markets.

## Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs [...] Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress made progress in 2025 toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. One measure—the GENIUS Act—was signed into law. [...] In the U.S., landmark legislation enacted in July 2025 has begun defining the roles of federal agencies in regulating stablecoins and digital commodities. Although implementation is ongoing, these laws represent a shift away from case-by-case enforcement and toward a structured national policy.
